clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12153, whose subject line describes decontrolling heavy oil. Section 1-101 exempts, effective August 17, 1979, prices charged in the first sale of heavy crude oil from price controls adopted under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 and defines heavy crude oil as crude oil of 16.0 degrees API gravity or less. Executive Order 12186 (1979-12-21) replaced the 16.0 figure with 20.0 degrees API (before: 16.0 degrees API or less; after: 20.0 degrees API or less) and Executive Order 12189 (1980-01-16) restated the order to read as follows, exempting heavy crude oil as defined by period: 16.0 degrees API or less for August 17 to December 20, 1979 and 20.0 degrees API or less from December 21, 1979. These are strike-and-insert amendments under owner ruling 2026-10-21; the clause continues, amended, and the rewrite changed the substance of the definition. No earlier express end was found.

Terminated by express deletion. Section 1-102 directed the Secretary of Energy to conduct a public inquiry on what other types of heavy crude oil should be exempt and to make a recommendation to the President. Executive Order 12186 of December 21, 1979 (44 FR 76477, Federal Register of December 27, 1979; held government printing) amends this order by deleting section 1-102; it states no effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1979-12-21 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). Executive Order 12189 (1980-01-16) restated the order without restoring the inquiry, and Executive Order 12553 of 1986-02-25 later revoked the order by number; both are later events because the clause had already ended. No earlier end was found.

The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12153, whose subject line describes decontrolling heavy oil. Section 1-103 lets the Secretary of Energy adopt regulations to implement the order under Executive Order 11790 as amended by Executive Order 12038. Executive Order 12186 renumbered it as section 1-102 (1979-12-21) and Executive Order 12189 restated it as section 1-104 (1980-01-16); these are amendments, later events, and the clause continues amended. No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12153 (44 FR 48949, Federal Register of August 21, 1979; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Decontrol of Heavy Oil and signed August 17, 1979. The dossier recorded the three numbered sections as one whole clause; they are separate commands with different fates (section 1-102 was deleted by a later order), so the inventory is corrected to sections 1-101, 1-102 and 1-103 using absolute spans of the held original. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12153, whose subject line describes decontrolling heavy oil. Section 1-102 ended earlier on 1979-12-21 by deletion; sections 1-101 and 1-103 end on 1986-02-25 and the whole-order end is the later date. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. Executive Order 12287 of January 28, 1981 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12287.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) exempted all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls adopted under that Act without naming this order; it is likewise a disclosed candidate earlier end and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in the printings of EO 12186, EO 12189. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
